title: solution.tex Lemma bound: trapezoid vertex labeling is internally inconsistent

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, paragraph 'The trapezoid estimate' (just before Lemma \ref{lem:bound}).

The vertices are written 'clockwise from bottom-left as $a_2,a_1,a_1',a_2'$ with $G(a_k)=a_k'$', and the same sentence asserts '$f$ identifies the lower-left vertex with the upper-right vertex'. These are inconsistent.

With $A$ running from bottom $(x_b,0)$ to top $(x_t,1)$ and $G(x,y)=(x+\beta,1-y)$, one computes $G(A)$ runs from $(x_b+\beta,1)$ (TOP-right) to $(x_t+\beta,0)$ (BOTTOM-right). Hence $G(a_2)$ (with $a_2$ = bottom-left point of $A$) is the **top-right** vertex, and $G(a_1)$ is the **bottom-right** vertex. So clockwise from bottom-left the correct order is $a_2,a_1,a_2',a_1'$ (as in problem.tex), NOT $a_2,a_1,a_1',a_2'$.

**Why this is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** With the printed (wrong) labeling, $a_1'=G(a_1)$ sits at top-right, so $C\subset\{y=1\}$ joins $a_1$ to $a_1'$, giving $f(C)$ from $f(a_1)$ to $f(a_1')=f(a_1)$ — a CLOSED LOOP. The proof of Lemma `bound` explicitly needs '$f(C)$ joins the two endpoints of $f(A)$', which is false under the wrong labeling. The same problem affects $D$.

**Fix.** Relabel clockwise as $a_2,a_1,a_2',a_1'$. Then $C$ joins $a_1$ to $a_2'$, so $f(C)$ joins $f(a_1)$ to $f(a_2')=f(a_2)$ = the two endpoints of $f(A)$; and $D$ joins $a_2$ to $a_1'$, so $f(D)$ joins $f(a_2)$ to $f(a_1')=f(a_1)$. With this relabeling the endgame's coordinate computation (C joins tops, D joins bottoms) and Lemma bound become consistent.
